authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: No Torpor Orb / Karn, Argent Defender (decisions L23, L27).
No Zombie tribal or Voltron drift (L22, L26, L60).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: The ETB needs three creatures, 3 life and gives an opponent three cards; without fodder he is sacrificed.
Edicts, exile and bounce get around indestructible.
Optional loops can deck you; stop before it happens.

value.interaction: Stubborn Denial, Not of This World, Swan Song, Feed the Swarm, Chaos Warp, Blasphemous Edict, Blasphemous Act.
value.mana: 34 land-capable slots with Cavern of Souls and Kher Keep; Sol Ring, Talismans, Nightscape Familiar.
value.protection: Lightning Greaves, Not of This World, indestructible.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Tresserhorn is the card-draw engine for every sacrifice, a Zombie for Gravecrawler, and a 10-power threat.
accepted_role.honest_note: Commander-native: 6 of the 21 Spellbook combos need him (The Locust God + an outlet + Tresserhorn), and he is the Zombie that lets Gravecrawler loop. The ETB gives an opponent three cards. Legality conflict for Cory: the source says the future-release exception is stale and the card is legal now (verification L48, L67; approvals L18), but the Scryfall cache used by the registry shows it not_legal (mbc, released 2026-10-19), and the Madcap Jester source gives 2026-11-13 for the same set. The registry keeps PENDING_RELEASE and the exception row; this blueprint changes neither.
